key_insight: Better uncertainty, calibration, or ranking diagnostics do not necessarily improve materials screening decisions or reduce DFT costs.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate reliability interventions by how much DFT verification they avoid while preserving required recall of near-hull candidates.
method: Evaluate MACE-MP, CHGNet, and Orb V3 for crystal-structure screening before DFT verification.
Test novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits against a decision-aligned objective.
Use two-oracle analysis to distinguish misaligned reliability targets from finite-budget audit limitations.
evidence_signal: Across all three interventions, diagnostic gains did not reliably improve screening; oracle analysis showed that model-selection value depended on whether screening used formation energies or hull-aligned predictions.
watch_item: Sparse audit-based routing was not robustly beneficial in the evaluated settings, so deployment gains require validation against the actual screening objective and information-acquisition cost.
paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
